content: The term Hollywood in drug slang refers to an exceptionally large and often hazardous single dose or line of cocaine. For most users, a standard line of cocaine typically contains between 50 to 75 milligrams of the substance. However, a Hollywood line can contain over 200 milligrams in a single dose, which significantly exceeds the usual amount. The origin of the term is linked to the highly publicized, excessive, and often indulgent cocaine use by celebrities and affluent individuals in the Hollywood area. This method of consumption is considered high-risk and far more dangerous than consuming the same total dosage in smaller increments over a longer period of time. Acute overuse of cocaine, such as through a Hollywood line, is a common cause of overdose. This can lead to severe complications, including cardiac arrhythmias, hyperthermia, and other issues related to increased heart rate, elevated blood pressure, and heightened adrenaline production. These physiological effects can be life-threatening. When large single doses of cocaine are taken intranasally (snorted), they are particularly irritating to the mucous membranes of the nasal passages. This irritation can accelerate the development of nasal ulcers and even perforations of the nasal septum, further compounding the risks associated with this method of drug use.
